name: return_immediately
description: Contains only a return instruction and performs no work. Its two unnamed callers get no effect from it.

name: clear_buffer_from_pointer
description: Saves the address held in its pointer register into a base-relative slot of a shared state block, then zeroes a fixed-length run of consecutive bytes starting at that address.

name: clear_flagged_table_entries
description: Zeroes a base-relative counter, then walks a flag table from the highest index down to zero, clearing every entry whose flag bit is set and passing over the rest.

name: clear_entry_and_decrement
description: Reads an index byte from the record passed in the address register. If the flag bit is set for that index in the flag table, it decrements a counter, then clears that table entry.

name: forward_call_and_return
description: Calls one unnamed routine with no arguments and returns straight after it. It adds no logic of its own.

name: dispatch_flagged_slot_methods
description: If the table flag for the record's index is clear, it walks an 8-byte slot list up to a stored limit, invoking the method of each slot whose status bit is set, then clears the entry. If the flag is set, it decrements a counter and clears the entry instead.

name: update_timed_object_state
description: Runs the slot-method dispatch, then counts down a timer field on the object record. On expiry it updates a 32-bit accumulator, may add a scaled value to a global total, resets record fields and calls a chain of routines; otherwise it sets a short delay field and calls a callback after a ratio check. The listing is cut off part way through, so the later branches are not fully visible.

name: call_function_pointer
description: Calls a function through a pointer stored in a base-relative table and returns a 64-bit value whose high half is one and whose low half is the second input register.

name: mark_record_and_invoke_hooks
description: Calls a function through a pointer, sets the low bit of a status byte in the record, then calls a second function pointer only when a state byte in the record equals minus one. Returns the constant one.

name: process_triggered_object_state
description: When a match byte equals the active value and the record's state flags allow it, it updates a 32-bit accumulator from a table lookup and resets several record fields before calling routines. It may repeat unnamed calls, with the counts drawn from a function, when the record's timer lies in a fixed range.

name: return_first_stack_argument
description: Returns the value passed on the stack, unchanged, and does no other work.

name: init_record_from_samples
description: Stores the low word of its first input into a record field, sets several state bytes and a counter, then adds two sampled values, scaled by shifts, into three 32-bit record fields. It finishes by calling a routine and returning its result.

name: update_counters_from_sample
description: Reads a sample from a function and compares it with a limit, then either decrements an indexed count and increments a total, or adds a table-driven amount to three 16-bit counters for the low and middle bands. Top-band samples clear an indexed slot; a flag-gated callback ends the routine.

name: extract_flag_from_mask
description: Draws an index from a function call and tests that bit in the record's 32-bit source mask, retrying while a returned word is nonzero. If a set bit is found, it moves that bit from the source mask to a destination mask.

name: classify_input_into_counter_bands
description: Sorts the input word into bands: the lowest band adds a table amount to three counters and clears a pending byte, the middle band does the same with a fixed offset, and the top band clears an indexed slot. Flag-gated callbacks run afterwards.

name: consume_pending_value_bonus
description: Reads and clears a pending index byte and a 32-bit record field. When the record's flag is set it adds a table-indexed amount to three counters, then calls two flag-gated callbacks.

name: apply_offset_pending_bonus
description: If the record's pending byte is nonzero, it sets that byte to one and, when the record flag is set, adds a table amount reduced by four to three counters. It then runs the same two flag-gated callbacks.

name: consume_bucket_for_value
description: Searches a threshold table by repeatedly subtracting its entries from the input word. When the input goes negative it decrements the matching bucket count and increments a total, then calls a flag-gated callback.

name: drain_motion_budget
description: Moves two record fields toward targets, then subtracts a cost, built from the magnitudes of three signed record fields scaled by a table entry, from a 32-bit budget field and returns that cost while budget remains. When the budget runs out it may draw on a global reserve, set a flag, or count down a field, then clears three record accumulators.

name: spend_budget_with_fallback
description: Subtracts a given amount from a 32-bit budget field in the record and returns while budget remains. When the budget is exhausted it zeroes the field, may spend a global reserve or set a flag, then clears three record accumulators.

name: move_reserve_into_budget
description: If a reserve counter in the shared block is nonzero, it moves one unit into a usage counter and adds a fixed amount to the record's 32-bit budget field. It then sets a status flag, calls a handler once if the flag was previously clear, and clears three record accumulators.

name: refill_budget_from_countdown
description: If a countdown byte in the record is nonzero, it decrements that byte and adds a fixed amount to the record's 32-bit budget field. It then clears three record accumulators.

name: set_flag_and_call_handler
description: Sets the low bit of a shared status byte and calls a handler through a pointer only if that bit was previously clear. It then clears three record accumulators.

name: tick_timer_and_dispatch
description: Subtracts a given amount from a 32-bit timer. When the subtraction runs past zero it reloads the timer with a fixed amount, decrements two counters, then runs a comparison chain that may credit a table amount to three counters and invoke a handler.

name: reload_timer_and_dispatch
description: Adds a fixed reload amount to a 32-bit timer, decrements two counters, and runs a comparison chain that may credit a table amount to three counters and invoke a handler. It has no initial subtraction, so it is only the reload path.

name: credit_pending_bonus_to_counters
description: If the record's pending byte is nonzero, it clears that byte and the record's 32-bit budget field, then adds a table amount to three counters. It then invokes a handler through a pointer.

name: credit_bonus_if_under_limit
description: Calls a routine and compares the low byte of its result with a counter. If the comparison passes and a pending byte is nonzero, it clears the pending state, adds a table amount to three counters, and invokes a handler.

name: credit_bonus_after_flag_check
description: Calls a routine, then if the processor zero flag it leaves set is true, compares a returned byte with a counter. If that passes and a pending byte is nonzero, it credits a table amount to three counters and invokes a handler.

name: switch_active_slot_method
description: Stores its word input in the active-slot field, first invoking the method of the slot named by the previous value when that value is nonzero. The new input is left stored in the field.

name: store_active_slot_index
description: Stores its word input into the active-slot field of the shared block and does nothing else.

name: lookup_range_scaled_value
description: Maps a 32-bit input to an offset into a shared 16-bit table by magnitude band, shifting the value to form the offset. It returns the looked-up entry scaled by a band-dependent shift.

name: initialize_slot_table
description: Resets the active-slot field, stores two fixed seed constants, and fills a slot table with pointers to handler routines and a shared data block. It then copies each slot's first long into its record and invokes the routine that the slot names.

name: initialize_and_run_slot_steps
description: Sets seed constants when the input word is below 1024, resets several timing fields to fixed values, then runs a pass over the slot list for each step from the input's low byte up to a fixed limit.

name: process_bit_two_entries
description: Clears three bits in a status byte and invokes a method on each slot with an active byte set. It compares two timer words against a fixed period, advances one of them by whole periods when that applies, and then walks the table from its top index down, calling a slot method for each entry whose bit two is set.

name: call_handlers_for_active_slots
description: Walks the slot list and, for each slot whose active byte is nonzero, calls the routine stored at a fixed method offset of that slot's descriptor.

name: dispatch_slots_matching_value
description: When the status flag is clear, it reads a value from a function and walks the slot list, invoking a method on each slot whose stored byte matches that value. It finishes by calling another function pointer.

name: call_handlers_by_bit_mask
description: Chooses a bit position from the input word by testing it against a few specific codes, defaulting to one. It then calls the method stored in each slot whose status byte has that bit set.

name: advance_pseudo_random_state
description: Advances a two-word state: the first word gains a rotated copy of the second word xored with a fixed constant, and the second word is replaced by a shifted and rotated copy of the old first word.

name: compute_scaled_random_value
description: Advances the same two-word state, then multiplies the low word of its first input by the upper half of the new state. It returns the product with its halves swapped, alongside the second input.

name: scale_input_by_mixed_state
description: Multiplies the low word of its first input by the upper half of a sum built from a rotated register value, that register value, and the second input, then returns the product with its halves swapped.

name: negate_64_bit_value
description: Calls a routine that returns a 64-bit value and returns its two's-complement negation, with the high half adjusted for the borrow from the low half.

name: multiply_difference_or_negate
description: Subtracts one 64-bit operand from another. When the high half of the difference is non-negative it multiplies the difference by a 32-bit operand and returns the normalised product; otherwise it calls a routine and returns that result negated.

name: multiply_32x32_to_64
description: Multiplies two 32-bit input operands by building the product from 16-bit partial products, adding the carries, and returns the result as a normalised 64-bit value.

name: build_scaled_vector_components
description: Derives two 16-bit differences from two routine results and stores them in the record, then computes scaled products of those differences and the second input. It shifts the products by a count input and stores six 32-bit vector components in the record.

name: store_vector_with_shifted_tail
description: Stores three 32-bit inputs as the first three components of a record vector, then stores three further inputs shifted left by the count input minus one as the last three components.

name: accumulate_scaled_vector
description: Scales three signed 16-bit record values by a 16-bit input, shifts each product by a count held in the record, and adds the results into three 32-bit vector components with carry propagation.

name: shift_result_by_bit_length
description: Counts how many bits the third input register holds, then calls a routine and shifts its 64-bit result left by that count plus one.

name: shift_result_by_halving_count
description: Halves the second input register until it fits within a signed 16-bit range while counting the shifts, then calls a routine and shifts its 64-bit result left by that count plus one.

name: negate_halves_separately
description: Calls a routine that returns a 64-bit value and returns it with each 32-bit half negated separately, without any borrow correction.

name: dispatch_scaled_multiply_path
description: Chooses one of three paths from the sign and size of the high input word: negating a routine's result, multiplying two 32-bit operands by a scaled copy of the low input, or shifting a routine's result by a bit-length count.

name: scale_pair_on_zero_flag
description: Uses the processor zero flag as its selector. When it is set it multiplies two 32-bit operands by a shifted copy of the low input; when it is clear it shifts a routine's result by a bit-length count.

name: multiply_pair_by_shifted_input
description: Shifts the low input right by seven bits. If the result is too large for a signed 16-bit operand it halves it repeatedly, calls a routine and shifts that result back up; otherwise it multiplies two 32-bit operands by the shifted value directly.

name: multiply_pair_and_round
description: Multiplies two 32-bit operands by the low word of the second input and returns both products halved, with their rounding bits carried into the result.

name: add_64bit_into_wide_accumulator
description: Calls a routine for a 64-bit value and adds it, with carry, into the low words of a six-word accumulator in the record. It also adds two further inputs and two record values into the upper words, carrying as needed.

name: call_two_routines_in_sequence
description: Calls two unnamed routines one after the other and returns, with no logic of its own. Its code is identical to two other entries in this bundle.

name: call_two_routines_in_sequence
description: Calls two unnamed routines one after the other and returns, with no logic of its own. Its code is identical to two other entries in this bundle.

name: call_two_routines_in_sequence
description: Calls two unnamed routines one after the other and returns, with no logic of its own. Its code is identical to two other entries in this bundle.

name: fetch_table_word_at_offset
description: Returns the 16-bit word stored in a shared table at the offset given by its word input.

name: set_table_pointers_from_inputs
description: Stores its two 32-bit inputs into two adjacent pointer fields of the shared block, which the table lookups read later.

name: reset_table_pointers_to_global
description: Points both table pointer fields of the shared block at the same global data block.

name: allocate_slot_index_entry
description: If the slot byte for the input index is unused and an allocation counter is below a fixed limit, it records the counter in that slot. It then stores an index and counter pair in a shared table and advances the counter by four.

name: allocate_buffer_entry_or_zero
description: If the allocation counter is below a fixed limit, it writes the counter into the buffer byte at the input index, stores an index and counter pair in a shared table, and advances the counter by four. Otherwise it returns zero.

name: write_byte_and_index
description: Stores the low byte of its second input into a buffer at the first input's offset, writes an index and value pair into a second table, and advances the counter held at the first pointer by four.

name: stub_empty_routine
description: The decompiler produced no body for this routine, so no logic can be recovered from it. Treat it as an empty stub.

name: check_inputs_against_limits
description: Compares two inputs with upper limits of 319 and 167 and fetches a corrected value when either is exceeded. It then calls a routine in either case.

name: forward_call_to_routine
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns. It contains no further logic.

name: check_fetched_pair_against_limits
description: Fetches a pair from a routine and compares it with upper limits of 319 and 167, then checks the two inputs against the same limits. It finishes by calling a routine.

name: check_fetched_value_bounds
description: Fetches a value from a routine and tests it against an upper limit of 319. When that limit is exceeded it tests a second value against 167 and calls further routines, and it always finishes with a final call.

name: apply_mask_flags_and_call
description: When bit 128 of the record's 32-bit mask is set, it sets two shared status bits, marks the record's state byte and flags, and calls a routine. Otherwise, when bit 8 is set, it sets one status bit and does the same record marking and call; if neither bit is set it returns unchanged.

name: set_flags_and_call
description: Sets two shared status bits, marks the record's state byte and flags, then calls a routine and returns its inputs unchanged.

name: set_flag_and_call
description: Sets one shared status bit, marks the record's state byte and flags, then calls a routine and returns its inputs unchanged.

name: credit_counter_when_mask_clear
description: When mask bit 1024 is clear, it adds four to either a shared counter or a record counter, depending on a record byte. It then marks the state byte and flags, calls two routines, and sets a shared status bit.

name: store_mask_and_credit_counter
description: Stores its second input as the record's 32-bit mask, adds four to either a shared counter or a record counter depending on a record byte, then marks the state byte and flags, calls two routines and sets a shared status bit.

name: set_object_state_and_flags
description: Adds four to a record counter, marks the record's state byte and flags, calls two routines, and sets a shared status bit.

name: call_if_record_in_range
description: When the record's field is below 79 and the second pointer differs from the record, it calls a routine. It then calls a function pointer if the word in the seventh register is below 18.

name: apply_weighted_record_update
description: Looks up a per-record entry by the input byte and, when that entry is set and the record's 32-bit budget is nonzero, scales a weighted sum of two record fields by table values. It applies the result through several routine calls and, for one record code in a given state, copies a six-longword vector from the shared block into the record before a final notification.

name: apply_table_step_to_counter
description: Picks a table value from a state-derived index. For one index range it adds a scaled amount to a record counter with saturation; for the other it multiplies by a shifted shared value first. It then calls a routine and returns its result shifted right by four.

name: add_saturating_scaled_amount
description: Calls a routine, then multiplies the low word of its first input by a shifted copy of another register and shifts the product by a table amount. It adds that into a record counter with saturation, then calls a routine and returns its result shifted right by four.

name: apply_weighted_update_flagged
description: Sets a record status bit and computes a weighted sum of two record fields using table values from the shared block. It then applies the result through the same routine sequence as the weighted record update, including the record-code copy and final notification.

name: apply_signed_weighted_update
description: Sets a record status bit and derives a weighted sum of record fields from one of two table pairs, chosen by the sign of a shared value. It then applies the result to a record counter and invokes routines for the matching record code.

name: apply_weighted_update_second_pair
description: Derives a weighted sum of two record fields from a second table pair, then applies it through the same routine sequence as its siblings: scaling a record counter, invoking routines for the matching record code, and copying a six-longword vector into the record when that code and state match.

name: store_vector_and_adjust_counter
description: When a shared activity word is nonzero and an input flag bit or a routine check passes, it stores six inputs into the record's vector, marks the record's code and state, and calls routines. It then adjusts a record counter according to two more input flag bits.

name: stub_empty_routine
description: The decompiler produced no body for this routine, so no logic can be recovered from it. Treat it as an empty stub.

name: trigger_labelled_pending_event
description: When a per-record pending byte is nonzero, it clears the byte and updates either a shared counter or a record counter. It then sets the record's type and state bytes, copies a text label into the record, stores an owner index, and calls routines, with an extra notification when the owner matches the active one.

name: initialize_record_with_mine_label
description: Increments a record counter, sets the record's type and state bytes, and copies the text label Mine into the record. It then invokes routines that register the record and store its owner index, and finishes with a final routine call.

name: initialize_record_with_missile_label
description: Sets the record's secondary field, copies the text label Missile into the record, stores the owner index, and invokes routines that register the record. It finishes with a final routine call.

name: finalize_record_type_and_owner
description: Calls a routine, then, if the record's type byte equals eleven and its tag byte is under forty, raises the tag to forty and copies an owner index. It stores the owner index into a second record, zeroes a field and calls a routine before a final call.

name: forward_single_routine_call
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns, with no logic of its own.

name: add_signed_fixed_values
description: Adds three inputs into the first three 32-bit components of a record vector, and adds each input's sign extension, with carry, into the upper three components.

name: match_code_to_slot_entry
description: Compares an input code with four stored slot codes. On a match it sets one of a few global values for codes fourteen to seventeen; otherwise it clears a fixed block of 16-bit words and records the code in a free slot, with the slot chosen by the code's range.

name: match_code_slot_entry_a
description: Matches an input code against stored slot codes, clearing a fixed block of 16-bit words and recording the code when no slot matches. It is a near copy of its neighbours that differs only in which comparisons come first, and the listing is tangled, so the exact mapping is not fully recoverable.

name: match_code_slot_entry_b
description: Matches an input code against stored slot codes, clearing a fixed block of 16-bit words and recording the code when no slot matches. It is a near copy of its neighbours that differs only in which comparisons come first, and the listing is tangled, so the exact mapping is not fully recoverable.

name: match_code_slot_entry_c
description: Matches an input code against stored slot codes, clearing a fixed block of 16-bit words and recording the code when no slot matches. It is a near copy of its neighbours that differs only in which comparisons come first, and the listing is tangled, so the exact mapping is not fully recoverable.

name: match_code_slot_entry_d
description: Matches an input code against stored slot codes, clearing a fixed block of 16-bit words and recording the code when no slot matches. It is a near copy of its neighbours that differs only in which comparisons come first, and the listing is tangled, so the exact mapping is not fully recoverable.

name: match_code_slot_and_call
description: Matches an input code against stored slot codes, sets global values for codes fourteen to seventeen, or clears a fixed block of 16-bit words and records the code in a free slot. It then calls three unnamed routines.

name: store_value_with_threshold
description: Stores the input word into a per-code global for the special codes and codes five to thirteen, after comparing it with that code's threshold and clearing a flag if it falls short. For codes fourteen to seventeen it sets fixed values instead, and otherwise it clears a fixed block of 16-bit words and records the code in a free slot.

name: store_value_from_index_six
description: Picks a threshold for the input index by a chain of comparisons that starts at index six, then stores the input word into the matching per-code global. Codes fourteen to seventeen set fixed values, and any other code clears a fixed block of 16-bit words and records the code.

name: store_value_from_index_seven
description: Picks a threshold for the input index by a chain of comparisons that starts at index seven, then stores the input word into the matching per-code global. Codes fourteen to seventeen set fixed values, and any other code clears a fixed block of 16-bit words and records the code.

name: store_value_from_index_eight
description: Picks a threshold for the input index by a chain of comparisons that starts at index eight, then stores the input word into the matching per-code global. Codes fourteen to seventeen set fixed values, and any other code clears a fixed block of 16-bit words and records the code.

name: store_value_from_index_nine
description: Picks a threshold for the input index by a chain of comparisons that starts at index nine, then stores the input word into the matching per-code global. Codes fourteen to seventeen set fixed values, and any other code clears a fixed block of 16-bit words and records the code.

name: store_value_from_index_ten
description: Picks the limit for the input index from a chain of comparisons that starts at index ten, then stores the input word into the matching per-code global. Codes fourteen to seventeen set fixed values, and any other code clears a fixed block of 16-bit words and records the code.

name: store_value_from_index_eleven
description: Picks the limit for the input index from a chain of comparisons that starts at index eleven, then stores the input word into the matching per-code global. Codes fourteen to seventeen set fixed values, and any other code clears a fixed block of 16-bit words and records the code.

name: store_value_with_default_limit
description: Compares the input word with a default limit and clears a flag if it falls short. It then stores the word into the per-code global and applies the same fixed-value and slot-clearing branches as its siblings.

name: store_value_default_limit_b
description: Compares the input word with a default limit and clears a flag if it falls short. It then stores the word into the per-code global and applies the same fixed-value and slot-clearing branches as its siblings, with a shorter call sequence.

name: store_value_with_limit_35
description: Compares the input word with the limit for code 35 and clears a flag if it falls short. It then stores the word into the per-code global and applies the same fixed-value and slot-clearing branches as its siblings.

name: store_value_with_limit_36
description: Compares the input word with the limit for code 36 and clears a flag if it falls short. It then stores the word into the per-code global and applies the same fixed-value and slot-clearing branches as its siblings, with a longer call sequence.

name: store_limit_for_code_11
description: Stores its word input as the limit for code 11, then runs the slot logic that clears a fixed block of 16-bit words and records the current code when no slot matches. It belongs to a family of routines that differ only in which limit they store.

name: store_limit_for_code_10
description: Stores its word input as the limit for code 10, then runs the slot logic that clears a fixed block of 16-bit words and records the current code when no slot matches. It belongs to a family of routines that differ only in which limit they store.

name: store_limit_for_code_9
description: Stores its word input as the limit for code 9, then runs the slot logic that clears a fixed block of 16-bit words and records the current code when no slot matches. It belongs to a family of routines that differ only in which limit they store.

name: store_limit_for_code_8
description: Stores its word input as the limit for code 8, then runs the slot logic that clears a fixed block of 16-bit words and records the current code when no slot matches. It belongs to a family of routines that differ only in which limit they store.

name: store_limit_for_code_7
description: Stores its word input as the limit for code 7, then runs the slot logic that clears a fixed block of 16-bit words and records the current code when no slot matches. It belongs to a family of routines that differ only in which limit they store.

name: store_limit_for_code_6
description: Stores its word input as the limit for code 6, then runs the slot logic that clears a fixed block of 16-bit words and records the current code when no slot matches. It belongs to a family of routines that differ only in which limit they store.

name: store_limit_for_code_5
description: Stores its word input as the limit for code 5, then runs the slot logic that clears a fixed block of 16-bit words and records the current code when no slot matches. It belongs to a family of routines that differ only in which limit they store.

name: store_limit_for_code_35
description: Stores its word input as the limit for code 35, then runs the slot logic that clears a fixed block of 16-bit words and records the current code when no slot matches. It belongs to a family of routines that differ only in which limit they store.

name: store_limit_for_code_36
description: Stores its word input as the limit for code 36, then runs the slot logic that clears a fixed block of 16-bit words and records the current code when no slot matches. It belongs to a family of routines that differ only in which limit they store.

name: set_fixed_values_for_codes
description: For codes fourteen to seventeen it sets fixed global values, and it sets the flag word when the index is in range. It then runs the slot logic that clears a fixed block of 16-bit words and records the current code when no slot matches.

name: set_fixed_value_by_index
description: Sets a fixed global value chosen by the index input when that index is fourteen to seventeen, then runs the slot logic that clears a fixed block of 16-bit words and records the current code when no slot matches.

name: set_fixed_value_from_fifteen
description: Sets a fixed global value chosen by the index input when that index is fifteen to seventeen, then runs the slot logic that clears a fixed block of 16-bit words and records the current code when no slot matches.

name: set_fixed_value_from_sixteen
description: Sets a fixed global value chosen by the index input when that index is sixteen or seventeen, then runs the slot logic that clears a fixed block of 16-bit words and records the current code when no slot matches.

name: set_fixed_value_from_seventeen
description: Sets a fixed global value when the index input is seventeen, then runs the slot logic that clears a fixed block of 16-bit words and records the current code when no slot matches.

name: set_fixed_values_from_fourteen
description: Sets a fixed global for index fourteen (32000), fifteen (1), sixteen (2) and seventeen (2), clearing a flag for any other index. It then runs the slot logic that clears a fixed block of 16-bit words and records the current code when no slot matches.

name: set_fixed_values_from_fifteen
description: Sets fixed globals for index fifteen (1), sixteen (2) and seventeen (2), clearing a flag for any other index. It then runs the slot logic that clears a fixed block of 16-bit words and records the current code when no slot matches.

name: set_fixed_values_from_sixteen
description: Sets fixed globals for index sixteen (2) and seventeen (2), clearing a flag for any other index. It then runs the slot logic that clears a fixed block of 16-bit words and records the current code when no slot matches.

name: set_fixed_values_at_seventeen
description: Sets one fixed global to two and clears a flag when the index is not seventeen. It then runs the slot logic that clears a fixed block of 16-bit words and records the current code when no slot matches.

name: claim_channel_slot_three
description: Claims the first free audio-channel slot for the current code, testing the slots in a fixed priority order and clearing a fixed block of 16-bit words for the chosen one. It touches the channel-three location register and clears the code register before returning.

name: claim_channel_slot_two
description: Claims the first free audio-channel slot for the current code, testing the slots in a fixed priority order and clearing a fixed block of 16-bit words for the chosen one. It touches the channel-two location register and clears the code register before returning.

name: claim_channel_slot_one
description: Claims the first free audio-channel slot for the current code, testing the slots in a fixed priority order and clearing a fixed block of 16-bit words for the chosen one. It touches the channel-one location register and clears the code register before returning.

name: claim_channel_slot_zero
description: Claims the first free audio-channel slot for the current code, testing the slots in a fixed priority order and clearing a fixed block of 16-bit words for the chosen one. It touches the channel-zero location register and clears the code register before returning.

name: release_audio_channel_slot
description: Tests the four audio-channel slot flags in priority order and clears the block of the first matching slot, recording the code and setting its mode value. When no slot matches it sets the mode value to 255 and clears the code register.

name: release_audio_channel_slot_b
description: Tests the four audio-channel slot flags in priority order and clears the block of the first matching slot, recording the code and setting its mode value. When no slot matches it sets mode one and clears the code register.

name: release_audio_channel_fallback
description: Tests three audio-channel slot flags in priority order, clearing the block of the first match and recording the code with its mode value. Used as a fallback when the wider slot search finds nothing.

name: release_audio_channel_pair
description: Tests two audio-channel slot flags in priority order, clearing the block of the first match and recording the code with its mode value. It falls through to a default mode when neither flag matches.

name: release_audio_channel_single
description: Tests one audio-channel slot flag and, when it matches, clears that slot's block and records the code with its mode value. Otherwise it clears the code register.

name: route_audio_channels
description: Compares a stored channel value with each of four channel slot codes and calls a routine for the first match. It then clears the channel value.

name: reset_audio_state
description: Sets a mode flag and calls a routine, then clears each of four fixed blocks of 16-bit words in turn, calling a routine between them. It ends by clearing the code register and the status flag.

name: set_mode_one_and_store
description: Sets a mode flag to one, stores its word input as a stored value, and sets a counter variable to 64.

name: set_mode_two_and_store
description: Sets a mode flag to two, stores its word input as a stored value, and clears a counter variable.

name: allocate_audio_channel_slot
description: Rejects an input value of zero or above 64, and a request that matches a busy channel. Otherwise it picks the first free slot from the four-channel set, or the slot with the smallest stored value when the candidates are all taken, then stores a pointer, a word and the constant 200 into that channel block and marks the slot active.

name: select_audio_channel_slot
description: Chooses an audio channel slot in the same way as the allocation routine, without its input range checks, then stores a pointer, a word and the constant 200 into the channel block and marks it active.

name: select_audio_channel_slot_b
description: Chooses an audio channel slot in the same way as the allocation routine, without its input range checks, then stores a pointer, a word and the constant 200 into the channel block, sets a flag around the call, and marks the slot active.

name: select_audio_channel_slot_c
description: Chooses an audio channel slot using the same priority rules as its siblings, stores a pointer, a word and the constant 200 into that channel block, and sets a status flag around the call. It then clears the status flag and updates the matching channel busy flag.

name: select_audio_channel_slot_d
description: Chooses an audio channel slot with a reduced set of priority tests, stores a pointer, a word and the constant 200 into the channel block, and sets a status flag around the call. It then updates the matching channel busy flag.

name: select_audio_channel_slot_e
description: Chooses the lowest-valued audio channel slot among the candidates, stores a pointer, a word and the constant 200 into its block, and sets a status flag around the call. It then updates the matching channel busy flag.

name: select_audio_channel_slot_f
description: Chooses an audio channel slot by comparing candidate values with the input word, stores a pointer, a word and the constant 200 into its block, and sets a status flag around the call. It then updates the matching channel busy flag.

name: store_channel_block_and_release
description: Stores a pointer, a word and the constant 200 into a channel block passed in an address register, sets a status flag, calls a routine with a stored index, and then releases the channel.

name: mark_channel_slot_status
description: Stores the channel status word into the block, then clears the busy flag for channel four, three, two or one, depending on the status value. It finishes by clearing the status flag.

name: clear_channel_busy_flag
description: Clears the busy flag for channel three when the status word is three, clears the flag for channel two when it is two, and otherwise clears the flag for channel one. It then clears the status flag.

name: clear_channel_busy_pair
description: Clears the busy flag for channel two when the status word is two, and otherwise clears the flag for channel one. It then clears the status flag.

name: reset_channel_one_flag
description: Clears the channel one busy flag, sets its companion flag to one, and clears the status flag.

name: call_two_routines_then_clear
description: Calls two unnamed routines and then clears the shared status flag. The text reference in the listing is not used by the code.

name: store_channel_request_block
description: Sets the request block's active word to one and clears the busy flag of the channel named in the block. It then stores the input registers and pointer into the block.

name: set_request_flags_and_store
description: Sets the request block's active word to one, clears a channel flag for the matching channel, and stores the input registers and a pointer into the block.

name: store_request_fields_for_two
description: Clears a channel flag when the fourth register holds two, sets the block's active word to one, and stores the input registers and a pointer into the block.

name: store_request_fields_plain
description: Clears one channel flag, sets the block's active word to one, and stores the input registers and a pointer into the block.

name: store_regs_to_block
description: Sets the block's active word to one, stores four input registers and a pointer into the block, and clears its final word.

name: write_channel_hardware_words
description: Clears the request block's fields and picks the hardware register block for the channel named in it, clearing the request block first when its flag is set. It then writes two words into that channel's hardware registers.

name: set_audio_channel_data
description: Picks the hardware register block for the channel named in the record, clearing the record first when its flag is set. It then writes two words from the record into that channel's hardware registers.

name: init_channel_tables
description: Clears a large shared state region. When the selector word is nonzero it loads four 32-bit table values for that selector into the channel state, then sets eight fixed index values and resets the status flags. It calls a routine when the selector equals ten.

name: init_channel_tables_b
description: Repeats the initialisation of its sibling: it clears the shared state region, loads four table values for a nonzero selector, sets eight fixed index values, and resets the status flags. It calls a routine when the selector equals ten.

name: init_channel_tables_c
description: Repeats the initialisation of its sibling: it clears the shared state region, loads four table values for a nonzero selector, sets eight fixed index values, and resets the status flags. It calls a routine when the selector equals ten.

name: init_channel_tables_d
description: Repeats the initialisation of its siblings: it clears the shared state region, loads four table values for a nonzero selector, sets eight fixed index values, and resets the status flags. It calls a routine when the selector equals ten.

name: init_channel_tables_e
description: Repeats the initialisation of its siblings: it clears the shared state region, loads four table values for a nonzero selector, sets eight fixed index values, and resets the status flags. It calls a routine when the selector equals ten.

name: init_channel_tables_f
description: Repeats the initialisation of its siblings: it clears the shared state region, loads four table values for a nonzero selector, sets eight fixed index values, and resets the status flags. It calls a routine when the selector equals ten.

name: init_channel_tables_g
description: Repeats the initialisation of its siblings: it clears the shared state region, loads four table values for a nonzero selector, sets eight fixed index values, and resets the status flags. It calls a routine when the selector equals ten.

name: init_channel_tables_h
description: Repeats the initialisation of its siblings: it clears the shared state region, loads four table values for a nonzero selector, sets eight fixed index values, and resets the status flags. It calls a routine when the selector equals ten.

name: tick_audio_channel_timers
description: Returns early when its status flag is set. Otherwise it advances a mode counter toward a target, ages each active channel counter and, once a counter passes fifty ticks, decrements its remaining value and calls a routine. It then goes through the four channel slots and calls handlers for any slot whose code matches the current channel state.

name: release_channel_flag_by_code
description: Clears the busy flag for the channel matching the input code (four, three, two or one) and calls routines for each matched case.

name: enable_audio_channel
description: Sets a shared channel-enable variable to one and calls a routine.

name: reset_channel_states
description: Calls a routine, clears the per-channel state for each channel whose flag is set, and loads a table entry indexed by a channel variable. It then clears that variable and a second word.

name: disable_audio_channel
description: Clears a shared channel-enable variable to zero and calls a routine.

name: enable_audio_channel_zero
description: Sets a shared channel-enable variable to one and calls a routine. The listing touches the channel-zero location register.

name: enable_audio_channel_b
description: Sets a shared channel-enable variable to one and calls a routine.

name: disable_channel_and_load_table
description: Calls a routine, loads a 32-bit table entry indexed by a stored channel value into a state word, then clears that channel value and a companion word.

name: clear_audio_channel_latch
description: Clears a shared variable to zero and calls a routine. The listing touches the channel-one location register.

name: enable_audio_channel_one
description: Sets a shared channel-enable variable to one and calls a routine. The listing touches the channel-one location register.

name: enable_audio_channel_c
description: Sets a shared channel-enable variable to one and calls a routine.

name: disable_channel_load_table_b
description: Calls a routine, loads a 32-bit table entry indexed by a second stored channel value into a state word, then clears that value and a companion word.

name: clear_audio_channel_latch_two
description: Clears a shared variable to zero and calls a routine. The listing touches the channel-two location register.

name: enable_audio_channel_two
description: Sets a shared channel-enable variable to one and calls a routine. The listing is short and shows only those two steps, although the instruction count is higher.

name: enable_audio_channel_d
description: Sets a shared channel-enable variable to one and calls a routine.

name: disable_channel_load_table_c
description: Calls a routine, loads a 32-bit table entry indexed by a stored channel value into a state word, then clears that channel value and a companion word.

name: clear_audio_channel_latch_three
description: Clears a shared variable to zero and calls a routine. The listing touches the channel-three location register.

name: enable_audio_channel_three
description: Sets a shared channel-enable variable to one and calls a routine. The listing touches the channel-three location register.

name: run_sound_sequence_step
description: Advances one channel's sound sequence. When its countdown reaches zero it reads the next command from the sequence list, dispatches the command through a jump table, updates the channel's period and volume counters, writes the resulting words into the channel's hardware block, and calls a routine.

name: process_sound_sequence_command
description: Reads a command word from the sequence list and dispatches it through a jump table. It stores the channel's next pointer and count and writes a word into the channel hardware block, then sets its pending state.

name: start_sound_sequence
description: Stores the first word of a sequence into the channel's count field and points the channel at the sequence list. It clears a volume word and writes a computed value into the channel hardware block.

name: dispatch_sound_sequence_event
description: Reads the next event from the channel's sequence pointer, dispatches its opcode through a jump table, and updates the channel's period, volume and pointer fields.

name: advance_sound_sequence_event
description: Steps the channel's sequence pointer back by one event, reads that event and dispatches its opcode through a jump table, then updates the channel's period, volume and pointer fields.

name: dispatch_sequence_event_clear_bit
description: Clears bit two of a shared status word, then runs the same sound-sequence event dispatch as its siblings. The listing touches the CIA port register that carries joystick and disk status bits.

name: dispatch_sequence_event_set_bit
description: Sets bit two of a shared status word, then runs the same sound-sequence event dispatch as its siblings. The listing touches the CIA port register that carries joystick and disk status bits.

name: load_sequence_and_dispatch
description: Loads a sequence pointer and two words from the event block, then runs the sound-sequence event dispatch and updates the channel's period and volume fields.

name: fetch_sequence_event_and_dispatch
description: Fetches the next event from a sequence list held in the channel state, advances that list pointer, and dispatches the event through a jump table.

name: store_sequence_pointer_and_dispatch
description: Stores a 32-bit value and a pointer in the channel state, then runs the sound-sequence event dispatch.

name: store_sequence_words_and_dispatch
description: Stores two 32-bit input words in the channel state, then runs the sound-sequence event dispatch.

name: store_sequence_triplet_and_dispatch
description: Stores three 32-bit input words in the channel state and sets a pending flag, then runs the sound-sequence event dispatch.

name: clear_sequence_word_and_dispatch
description: Clears a word in the channel state and runs the sound-sequence event dispatch.

name: clear_sequence_flag_and_dispatch
description: Clears a flag word in the channel state and runs the sound-sequence event dispatch.

name: select_channel_for_command
description: Maps a command value of five, six, seven or eight to one of the four channel slots, then sets that slot's value and its status flags. Other values fall through to the default slot.

name: enable_channel_zero_flags
description: Sets the channel-zero status flags and clears its slot marker. The listing touches the channel-zero period and volume registers.

name: enable_channel_one_flags
description: Sets the channel-one status flags and clears its slot marker. The listing touches the channel-one period and volume registers.
